items.title: Myra Menville Interview, 1958-05-07, 09
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...as they were thinking in, you see, in Beethoven or Bach.

ctx.x: I'd say from the, let's say, middle classes, which takes in a very larger number now than ever before. People that are well behaved and soft spoken, some education, regardless of background or extraction, they're the coming America. And they have to be considered in this discussion. And I think their general acceptance is much more than those that are highly trained or specialized in any line. Coming back to the social side, they say the blue noses, blue bloods.

Well, in summer then you could say that New Orleans throughout the years have used it as a form of entertainment for... used jazz as a form of entertainment for music, I mean for dances and such like. They would, uh, some of them value in it as music, for instance, as they were thinking in, you see, in Beethoven or Bach. That would say, nobody, for the most part, would see any value in the music, but, uh, except as entertainment. And as entertainment was used, it has been used widely. Would you say that?
